comparisons.peer_topic: Definition and accounting treatment of nonperforming loans and leases
comparisons.peer_summary: Nonperforming loans and leases generally include those on nonaccrual status, excluding fair value option loans and LHFS. When deemed uncollectible, loans are charged off against the allowance for credit losses, with subsequent recoveries reversed through the same allowance, reported net of charge-offs.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures define the accounting treatment for charge-offs and net charge-offs against the allowance. Goldman Sachs specifies that net charge-offs for wholesale loans were not material in 2024, focusing on the composition of its loan portfolio, whereas Bank of America provides the general policy that loans deemed uncollectible are charged off against the allowance and that net charge-offs are reported net of recoveries.

sentences.text: Net charge-offs for wholesale loans were not material for 2024 and were primarily related to corporate loans for 2023.
When a nonaccrual loan is deemed uncollectible, it is charged off against the allowance for credit losses.
Charge-offs are reported net of recoveries (net charge-offs).

comparisons.peer_summary: The allowance for corporate loans, including modified loans, is based on the borrower's overall financial performance, and charge-offs for uncollectible amounts may be recorded at the time of modification or in prior periods.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address charge-offs related to corporate loans. Goldman Sachs notes that its 2023 net charge-offs were primarily related to corporate loans, while Citigroup details that for corporate loans, including modified loans, the allowance is based on borrower financial performance and charge-offs may be recorded at modification or in prior periods.

comparisons.peer_topic: Loans Held for Investment Valuation Basis
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans held for investment are reported at amortized cost, which consists of the outstanding principal balance adjusted for charge-offs, allowance for credit losses, and unamortized deferred fees, costs, premiums, or discounts.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures reference the amortized cost basis and the adjustment for charge-offs in the context of holding loans for investment. Goldman Sachs calculates the net charge-off ratio using average gross loans accounted for at amortized cost, while Morgan Stanley defines loans held for investment as reported at amortized cost adjusted for charge-offs and the allowance.

sentences.text: In the table above, the net charge-off ratio is calculated by dividing the net charge-offs by average gross loans accounted for at amortized cost.

Loans held for investment are reported at amortized cost, which consists of the outstanding principle balance adjusted for any charge-offs, the allowance for credit losses, any unamortized deferred fees or costs for originated loans, and any unamortized premiums or discounts for purchased loans.
